expanded_sentences: The patient is a 58-year-old male with a history of severe myocardial infarction, having experienced multiple infarctions that necessitated emergency stenting and subsequent bypass surgery.
The patient has been managing type 2 diabetes mellitus with metformin, maintaining HbA1c levels between 6.5% and 7.2%.
Elevated hepatic transaminase levels have been present since age 50, potentially due to statin therapy or non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
The patient has a history of hypercholesterolemia with LDL levels exceeding 190 mg/dL despite lifestyle interventions.
The patient was a smoker for 20 years, accumulating 20 pack-years, and quit smoking at age 45.
The patient has been diagnosed with stage III coronary artery disease, characterized by multivessel involvement and impaired left ventricular function.
A heart biopsy taken during bypass surgery revealed ischemic cardiomyopathy.
Genetic testing confirmed a heterozygous LDLR mutation, consistent with familial hypercholesterolemia.
The patient is currently on atorvastatin 40 mg orally and metformin 500 mg.
The patient's father died of sudden cardiac death at age 62.
